defects.claim_says: The parent's termination provision for the Commission, restated by later amending orders to October 3, 2001 ... is disclosed as a spent-fact candidate and the order stays on the books until the express revocation (citing the owner's 2026-10-21 reasoning)
defects.source_says: The 2026-10-21 report-deadline ruling covers report-relative endings and states 'a clause with its own fixed date is unaffected'. The parent's sunset is a fixed date: EO 13046 'NBAC shall terminate on October 3, 1999, unless extended by the President prior to that date', moved by EO 13137 sec. 3(c) to 'October 3, 2001'. No held extension exists, and EO 13316 lists the order among those that established committees that 'have terminated or whose work is completed'. The fixed own-terms sunset, 2001-10-03, is a dated earlier end that the claim dismisses on a ruling that excludes it. The claim does not resolve it, and 2003-09-30 is unsupported as the first end.

defects.claim_says: A by-number search of held order texts finds EO 13316 and the later orders that amend the parent citing the parent as amended by this order
defects.source_says: cruden.py number EO:13018 returns only EO 13316 (FR and APP) and EO 13018's own text; no later amending order cites 13018 by number (EO 13137 says only 'Executive Order 12975, as amended').

reasoning: Identity, quotes and the one-sentence inventory are correct, and EO 13316 does expressly revoke EO 12975 'as amended by Executive Orders 13018, 13046, and 13137', effective September 30, 2003. The earlier-end test fails on the merits. The Commission whose size this order sets had a fixed sunset written into the parent, October 3, 2001 as last amended, 'unless extended', and no extension is held. The claim sets the sunset aside by analogy to the report-deadline ruling, but that ruling expressly leaves fixed-date clauses unaffected. The claim needs either evidence of an extension or an end at the sunset (2001-10-03, with the revocation as a later event). The search result is also overstated.

The one-paragraph order amends section 1 of EO 13038 (member limit 'up to 25'; Co-Chairs). EO 13138, effective September 30, 1999, expressly revokes EO 13038 as amended by 13065 by number. The parent's termination is report-relative ('30 days after submitting its report'), and the report-deadline ruling and its stated extension to report-relative sunsets treat it as a spent fact, not an end, so the express revocation is the first end. EO 13081 is correctly a later event. The OFR note 'nullified by virtue of the Committee being abolished by EO 13138' agrees. Searches and savings are accurate.

evidence_checked: CATALOG_INDEX.csv EO:13068 (1997-11-25, 62 FR 63247; no disposition note)
reasoning: Three sections, all tied to Friday, December 26, 1997: the closing, the agency-head exception, and the treatment of the day under EO 11582 and 5 U.S.C. 5546 and 6103(b). The inventory is complete. Each ends by its own terms on 1997-12-26, inclusive with the exclusive reading disclosed, and the whole-order end equals the latest first end. No later instrument names the order, the search descriptions match the packet, and the savings statement is accurate.

Four sections: the half-day closing on December 24, 1998, the exception, the pay-and-leave treatment, and section 4 limiting the order to federal agencies. The inventory is complete. Each operates only on that day; section 4 is correctly treated as a scope limit ending with the closing. End 1998-12-24, inclusive. The searches are accurately described.

evidence_checked: EO_13225.txt (sec. 3(c) 'Executive Order 13090, as amended by Executive Order 13136'; sec. 5 'effective September 30, 2001')
EO_13090.txt (sec. 2(c) report date; sec. 3(d) terminate 60 days after final report)
cruden.py number EO:13136 (EO 13225 FR and APP, own text)
reasoning: The order moves the final-report date in EO 13090 section 2(c) from March 1, 1999 to December 31, 2000. The parent's termination is report-relative (60 days after the final report), which the report-deadline ruling treats as a spent fact, so the first end is EO 13225's express revocation by number, effective September 30, 2001. The amended date is a deadline, not an end. The search note that 'EO 13090 itself' was found is loosely worded (the number search finds only EO 13225 and this order's text), but it changes no fact on which the claim relies.

defects.claim_says: The restated termination date of October 3, 2001 is an earlier candidate: no held source shows an extension ... so under the owner's 2026-10-21 reasoning (the order stays on the books until revoked) it is disclosed as a spent fact and not recorded as the end; first end 2003-09-30
defects.source_says: This order's own section 3(c) sets the Commission's fixed termination: new section 8(b) is amended by deleting 'October 3, 1999' and inserting 'October 3, 2001' (the sentence as restated by EO 13046 reads 'NBAC shall terminate on ... unless extended by the President prior to that date'). The 2026-10-21 report-deadline ruling says 'a clause with its own fixed date is unaffected', so it does not support treating a fixed sunset as a spent fact. No extension is held, and EO 13316 recites that the listed committees 'have terminated or whose work is completed'. The fixed own-terms end of 2001-10-03 is not resolved; the 2003-09-30 first end for every clause, including section 3(c) itself, is unsupported.

evidence_checked: jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13137.txt (re-hashed; all eight spans match; read in full)
EO_13237.txt (new President's Council on Bioethics, November 2001; does not name EO 12975)
reasoning: Identity and the eight-clause inventory are complete and accurately quoted, and EO 13316 does revoke EO 12975 as amended by 13137, effective September 30, 2003. But the order itself fixes the Commission's termination at October 3, 2001 unless extended. That is a fixed own-terms date, and the owner's report-deadline ruling expressly excludes such dates, so the claim's reason for discarding it misstates the ruling. Without held evidence of an extension, the clauses, which structure and sustain the Commission, have a dated earlier end of 2001-10-03 that must be adopted or rebutted with evidence. The claim's search note ('finds only EO 13316 citing the parent as amended by this order') is accurate.

defects.claim_says: One clause EO:13184#whole whose original_operative_text and source span (chars 676-947) are the authority recital ending 'it is hereby ordered as follows:'
defects.source_says: The operative command follows at chars 947 onward: 'Executive Order 12834 of January 20, 1993, ''Ethics Commitments by Executive Branch Appointees,'' is hereby revoked, effective at noon January 20, 2001. Employees and former employees subject to the commitments in Executive Order 12834 will not be subject to those commitments after the effective date of this order.' Neither the revocation nor the release sentence is in any clause, so the inventory omits the order's only operative commands, while the judgment_reason relies on text outside the clause span.

evidence_checked: jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13184.txt (re-hashed; quoted spans match; offsets 676-947 and following read)
reasoning: The lifecycle conclusion (a self-executing revocation exhausted at noon January 20, 2001, its consequence an accrued effect) is reasonable. But the claim adopts the machine clause unchanged, and that clause covers only the authority recital. The review standard requires every operative command to be a clause, and here both operative sentences are outside the inventory. An inventory override that adds the revocation and release sentences is needed. No earlier end or later instrument naming the order was found.

Three sections tied to Monday, December 24, 2001, with a complete inventory, each ending by its own terms on that day, inclusive. The single OFR catalog hit is the 'See: EO 11582' cross-reference, correctly identified as an earlier instrument and not an event. Searches and savings are accurate.

defects.claim_says: The one machine hit for this order in the Office of the Federal Register catalog search names EO 11582, which this order cites in its own text as signed February 11, 1971
defects.source_says: The packet's machine search for EO 13281 records later-events:ofr_catalog machine_hits_for_this_order = 0, the catalog row for EO 13281 has no disposition note, and EDGES.csv has no edge for EO 13281. The described hit does not exist; the search is not honestly described (the sentence matches the one written for EO 13238, 13320 and 13343, which do have that hit).

reasoning: The legal analysis is correct: the half-day closing on Tuesday, December 24, 2002, the exception and the pay-and-leave treatment are a complete inventory, each ending on that day. But the rationale and earlier-end check report a catalog hit naming EO 11582 that the recorded search does not contain. Under the instruction that searches be adequate and honestly described, a false description of a search result is a ground for rejection even though the outcome is right.

defects.source_says: EO 13320 is 'of December 9, 2003' and closes agencies 'on Friday, December 26, 2003'; every judgment_reason, the savings text and the rationale give 2003-12-26. An end three years before the order's signing is impossible and inconsistent with the claim's reasons.

reasoning: The inventory (three sections) and own-terms analysis are correct, and the search descriptions match the packet. The date fields, 2000-12-26, are wrong: the order's day is December 26, 2003, as the claim's text states throughout. Reject for wrong and internally inconsistent dates.

Two sections: section 1 closes agencies on June 11, 2004 as a mark of respect for Ronald Reagan and treats the day under EO 11582 and the pay statutes; section 2 excepts offices kept open. The inventory is complete. Both end by their own terms on 2004-06-11, inclusive. The single catalog hit is the EO 11582 cross-reference, correctly described. No later instrument names the order.
